note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 4-weeks postpartum woman with sudden-onset shortness of breath at rest and pleuritic chest soreness; high concern for pulmonary embolism (PE). Urgent hospital evaluation advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint/timeline: Acute shortness of breath began about 1 hour prior to call while sitting and watching TV. New dry cough since yesterday.
- Associated symptoms: Palpitations (“heart really going”); chest soreness with deep inspiration. Denies chest pain at rest. Feels stressed. No sputum reported.
- Pertinent negatives mentioned: No chest pain at rest; no current codeine use in the past week. No respiratory illness in baby.
- Past medical/surgical history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago. Denies other medical problems.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (reaction unspecified).
- Medications: Codeine used regularly post-op; none taken for ~1 week.
- Family history: Mother had leg clots (DVT).
- Social: Postpartum at home with baby; partner at work.

Examination:
- Telehealth assessment only; no formal physical exam recorded.
- Vitals: Home radial pulse count 30 beats over an unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as slightly tachycardic. No SpO2, BP, respiratory rate, or temperature documented.
- No additional physical findings recorded.

Impression:
- Working impression: Suspected pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring urgent evaluation.
  - Supporting: Acute SOB at rest; pleuritic-type chest soreness with deep inspiration; 4 weeks postpartum after C-section (high VTE risk); perceived tachycardia; family history of DVT.
- Alternative considerations (top 2–3):
  - Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis: New cough since yesterday, but abrupt dyspnea at rest less typical; no fever/sputum documented.
  - Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea: Reports stress and palpitations; does not fully account for pleuritic soreness or postpartum VTE risk.

Plan:
- Urgent care: Patient advised to go to the hospital promptly for evaluation to rule out PE and other serious causes of dyspnea.
- Transport: Ambulance option discussed; patient elected self-transport with baby and was advised to go promptly and bring necessary supplies.
- Medications: Avoid taking codeine for now.
- Follow-up: To be determined by hospital findings and care team.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Full vital signs (SpO2, BP, respiratory rate, temperature).
  - Detailed reaction to ibuprofen; comprehensive medication list.
  - Review for DVT symptoms (unilateral leg pain/swelling), hemoptysis, syncope, fever, recent travel/immobility, smoking status, COVID-19 exposure, orthopnea/PND/edema.
  - Clear severity/functional impact of dyspnea; breastfeeding status not discussed.
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - DOB discrepancy: Patient stated 04/20/1980; clinician later said 1983 (conflict noted).
  - Pulse count timing unspecified; “slightly fast” interpretation noted without a calculated heart rate.
● Transcript quality:
  - Telehealth limitations with no objective vitals; some incomplete statements and limited ROS; otherwise understandable.
